title: XPX Security with Simultaneous Related-Key Offsets
summary: Existing XPX analysis covers primitive-dependent related-key maps with at most one nonzero offset; analyzing security when both offsets may be nonzero remains open.

formal_statement.body: For XPX with underlying permutation $P$, extend the related-key security analysis from the primitive-dependent KDF family $\Phi_{\oplus}^{P}$ of maps $\varphi_{\delta,\varepsilon}(k)=P^{-1}(P(k)\oplus\varepsilon)\oplus\delta$, restricted by $\delta=0\lor\varepsilon=0$, to the full family obtained by removing this side condition and thus permitting $\delta$ and $\varepsilon$ to be nonzero simultaneously. The open task is to analyze XPX security in this enlarged related-key model.

scope.domain: XPX related-key security for primitive-dependent KDF families in block-cipher design.
parameters: P: the underlying permutation used by XPX and the KDF maps
k: the key input to a related-key map
delta and epsilon: XOR offsets that may both be nonzero in the enlarged family
scope.unresolved_remainder: Analyze XPX related-key security for the full primitive-dependent KDF family after removing the restriction that at most one offset is nonzero.

citations.label: XPX: Generalized Tweakable Even-Mansour with Improved Security Guarantees

progress.summary: The paper analyzes XPX under a side condition allowing only one of the two KDF offsets to be nonzero. It presents removal of that condition as theoretically interesting but technically demanding for the security analysis.
citation_labels: Bart Mennink et al., XPX: Generalized Tweakable Even-Mansour with Improved Security Guarantees
